text: True or False: on a pseudo-Riemannian manifold, the Levi-Civita connection is the unique connection that is both torsion-free (Γ^ρ_μν = Γ^ρ_νμ) and metric-compatible (∇_ρ g_μν = 0).
explanation: True. This is the fundamental theorem of (pseudo-)Riemannian geometry stated in the book: a metric determines exactly one torsion-free, metric-compatible connection, whose Christoffel symbols are fixed by the metric. A manifold admits infinitely many connections in general, but these two conditions select a single one. Metric compatibility makes parallel transport preserve lengths and angles, and torsion-freedom gives the symmetry Γ^ρ_μν = Γ^ρ_νμ.
